judgments.reasoning_cat1: The aggregate provision is printed with a stray column fragment inside subparagraph (1) ('assumed (c) under any incidental contract') and a floating line of the introductory sentence, so the enumerated categories do not read continuously.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It replaces the coverage part's aggregate structure (c132), which remains printed, and depends on the schedule figures that do not match the declarations (c164).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Continuous or repeated exposure to substantially the same general condition ... one occurrence' is the classic number-of-occurrences formula that parties litigate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates the closing sentence of the superseded limits provision (c132) and stands beside the different aggregation rule for 'medical incident' in the HPL part (c046).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Loading or unloading' with a mechanical-device proviso is a much-construed definition, and it is expressed entirely in terms of 'property'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Form 009-050 (c188) provides that 'the loading or unloading of patients shall be considered health care services', so the two provisions treat the same phrase quite differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The offer-to-pay cut-off is stated clearly; 'that part of the judgment the Company pays' is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It adds to Supplementary Payments (c002), which already provides post-judgment interest, without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'For which the insured may be held liable as an employer or in any other capacity' is a deliberately sweeping phrase, and the substituted paragraphs are lettered inconsistently (a), (ii), (iii).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It deletes 'the exclusion relating to bodily injury to any employee of the insured' without identifying the coverage part, so its effect on HPL exclusion (a) (c039) and on the employee-injury proviso in c056 is unclear.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise 50-foot railroad proximity test with a stated carve-back; concrete.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It amends exclusion (5) of the Broad Form contractual liability coverage (c135), which is itself printed in run-together form.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The endorsement recites a statute rather than stating the amended territory language, leaving it unclear how the Policy Territory provision now reads.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 10 deletes Form 009-118 (10/92) as 'null and void' and substitutes the 2/96 version (c203, c205), yet this superseded form remains in the policy with a differently worded statutory recital.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Those individuals and/or entities to whom this coverage applies and that are not subject to the Wisconsin Patients Compensation Fund' is a vague class, and the increased limits are stated as a bare fraction ($1,000,000/$3,000,000).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The declarations and the HPL schedule state $400,000 each medical incident with a $1,000,000 (or $4,000,000) aggregate (c044), and the medical staff endorsement says no endorsement shall increase the declared limits (c187).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'If the need to increase the professional limits of liability ... is ever required, then the Company at its sole option may make an appropriate premium charge' is circular and leaves 'appropriate' wholly at the insurer's discretion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits with the increased limits in c173 and the premium computation condition (c020), which requires premiums to follow the company's rules and rating plans.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The indemnity is conditioned on it being 'determined that payment of said loss shall be rendered under this policy', without saying who determines or when, and the proportionality sentence is compressed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It operates alongside the Other Insurance Condition (c027) and the several excess clauses (c155, c157, c186), which are the very provisions that generate the inter-insurer disputes it addresses.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, clear statement that the coverage is claims made and requires a claim during the endorsement period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The rest of the policy is occurrence-based (c015, c038) and a Total Pollution Exclusion is also attached (c189-c192), so it is contestable whether any pollution cover survives.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It defines the retroactive date as 'the earliest date of any occurrence for which claims for damages may be made' in a claims-made endorsement, mixing occurrence and claim triggers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to 'the first named insured', a term used nowhere else in a policy that speaks of the 'named insured' (c013) and lists many named insureds (c092).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Subject to the terms of the policy which are not inconsistent herewith' invites argument about which policy terms yield, and the grant covers only discharges 'neither expected nor intended by the insured'.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Total Pollution Exclusion (c189-c191) excludes pollution liability at or from premises owned or occupied by any insured and all clean-up demands, which would negate the very cover this endorsement grants.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any solid, liquid, gaseous or thermal irritant or contaminant, including ... chemicals and waste' is famously broad, but here it defines a grant rather than an exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The identical definition appears in the Total Pollution Exclusion (c192), where it serves the opposite purpose, so the same words both grant and exclude.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence carve-out cross-referring to an identified endorsement; definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Nuclear Energy Liability Exclusion is in fact attached (c198-c201), so the cross-reference holds.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Costs' is expressly defined and the deductible and limits are stated in figures; little interpretive play.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Limits including costs is a different structure from Supplementary Payments (c002), which pays defence costs in addition to limits, an asymmetry that has to be recognised.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Claims which occur during the period of this endorsement or any retroactive date thereof' conflates claims with occurrences and is garbled, and an 'unlimited' endorsement whose aggregate is capped is internally odd.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It promises issue within ninety days of non-renewal or cancellation, which must be read with the cancellation and non-renewal regimes (c069, c106-c111).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Cover only 'while acting' in an administrative capacity, as instructor/supervisor of students, or as a committee member, is a scope test that is easy to dispute in a hospital setting.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same medical staff are addressed by paragraph (f) of the Wisconsin persons insured form (c058) on different terms, and paragraph 2 of this endorsement (c185) removes professional services cover that the HPL grant (c038) otherwise provides.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single sentence disapplying exclusion (c) for a defined group; clear in itself.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exclusion (c) remains printed (c041) and is already declared inapplicable in full by the Wisconsin persons insured endorsement (c060), so this partial disapplication is redundant or inconsistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Except in the instruction or supervision of students' carves an exception into an exclusion of professional health care services, and where administrative acts shade into clinical ones the line is genuinely uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It conflicts in practical effect with paragraph (f) of the persons insured form (c058) and with the unlicensed physicians endorsement (c037), which treat rotating and administrative physicians as covered.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short excess clause; 'other valid and collectible insurance' is a standard phrase.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It qualifies the Other Insurance Condition declaring this policy primary (c027) without expressly amending it, as the Broad Form excess clauses do (c155, c157).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence preserving the declared limits; unambiguous on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Patients Compensation Fund endorsement expressly increases the professional liability limits above the declarations (c173) and Form 041 applies the limits separately to three entities (c193), both of which are hard to square with this sentence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The endorsement says it amends exclusion (d) but the substituted text is lettered '(a)', a mechanical mislabel, and the deeming sentence ('loading or unloading of patients shall be considered health care services') sits inside an exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 5 amends this same form again for air ambulances (c071), the original exclusion (d) remains printed (c042), and the loading/unloading definition elsewhere is confined to property (c168).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An instruction identifying the replaced exclusion by description rather than letter, but the description matches exclusion (f) closely enough.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It removes the 'sudden and accidental' exception in c121 while a separate Pollution Liability Endorsement (c176-c182) grants pollution cover, leaving the policy with both a total exclusion and a bought-back coverage.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A detailed four-limb exclusion with a hostile-fire carve-back; comprehensive but each limb is specific.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Limbs (a) and (b) exclude precisely the owned-or-occupied premises pollution that the Pollution Liability Endorsement insures (c178), a direct clash within one instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clean-up cost exclusion is stated in two concrete limbs.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It excludes attendant clean-up costs that the Pollution Liability Endorsement expressly covers for another party's property (c178).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The standard broad pollutants definition; each listed substance is concrete though the category is wide.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Identical wording defines the grant in the Pollution Liability Endorsement (c179), so the same definition serves opposite functions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It says limits apply separately 'with respect to each of the following locations' and then lists three corporate entities, not locations — a mismatch that changes how the limits multiply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It multiplies the HPL limits stated in the declarations and coverage part (c044) and cannot easily coexist with the rule that endorsements shall not increase the declared limits (c187) or with the increased PCF limits (c173).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The text is broken mid-sentence with clauses transposed to the end, so the operative exclusion ('shall be limited to actual compensatory damages') cannot be read continuously, and 'damages' is then redefined to exclude plaintiff's legal fees.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 10 declares Form 009-133 'deleted from the policy and considered null and void' (c203), yet this form remains in the assembled policy.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It applies to products handled 'on, from or in connection with the use of any premises described in this endorsement' although the endorsement describes no premises or operations, so the trigger has no referent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It rewrites the jacket definition of 'products hazard' (c017) by dropping the away-from-premises requirement, so two versions of the defined term operate in the same instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Charitable health care services in their communities' is undefined and open-ended, and the deeming sentence has consequences for the employment-related exclusions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It duplicates Endorsement No. 9 (c090) word for word and, by deeming community acts to be in the course of employment, engages the employee-injury proviso in c056 and the employee exclusion (c039, c170).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It adds a paragraph (g) defined by reference to 'Section (d) of this endorsement', but paragraph (d) belongs to Form 009-109, not to this endorsement.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The same paragraph (g) is added by Endorsement No. 9 (c091), and paragraph (d) of Form 009-109 excludes Wisconsin-licensed physicians (c056), so the extended class is uncertain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Statutory and industry references make the exclusion technical but precise.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Cross-referenced and preserved by the pollution endorsement (c180) and by Fire Legal Liability's carve-out (c153); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow, concretely worded medical payments/first aid exclusion.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Aligns with the first-aid provisions in c002, c049 and c158; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Three specific limbs with a geographic proviso; the lettering is garbled but the substance is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with paragraphs A and B of the same endorsement; no clash located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definitions borrowed from the Atomic Energy Act with numerical thresholds; technical but definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The final line extends 'property damage' to all radioactive contamination, enlarging the jacket definition (c018) for this endorsement only — an intended, stated variation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate attachment language.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Endorsement No. 10 is dated 06/21/1996 but is expressed to be effective at inception; a mild but common mismatch.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Both deleted forms — the Trebled Damages Exclusion (c194) and the 10/92 policy territory endorsement (c172) — remain physically in the assembled policy, so the document contains provisions it declares null and void.
